selectedPublication.publicationTitle: Conflicts of interest and fair customer treatment in private markets

topChunk.publicationTitle: Conflicts of interest and fair customer treatment in private markets
topChunk.chunkText:
The scope of this review included firms managing funds or providing portfolio management and/or advisory services in the UK involving private equity, private credit and real estate assets.

We assessed whether firms' conflicts of interest frameworks and governance arrangements were sufficiently robust to identify, manage, mitigate and disclose conflicts of interest and whether they supported the fair treatment of investors.

results.question: What does published supervisory data show about UK mortgage portfolios exposed to flood risk?

selectedPublication.publicationTitle: Flood risk exposure of mortgages in England

topChunk.publicationTitle: Flood risk exposure of mortgages in England
topChunk.chunkText:
This analysis provides an overview of the exposure of mortgage lending to flood risk in England.

We found that around 1 in 7 mortgage contracts are linked to postcodes with some level of flood risk, although exposure varies by region and type of flooding.  The findings show that physical climate risks are relevant to mortgage markets because they affect consumers, firms, and market functioning.

selectedPublication.publicationTitle: DP26/1: Credit unions: review of the regulatory regime

topChunk.publicationTitle: DP26/1: Credit unions: review of the regulatory regime
topChunk.chunkText:
There are opportunities to support competition, innovation and the long-term sustainability of the sector.

The current framework provides appropriate support and safeguards in certain areas.

Credit unions have adequate tools to exit the market in an orderly manner.

We’re interested in hearing views on specific areas of the regulatory framework as well as how different approaches may operate together to support the sustainable development of the sector.

These proposals support our objective of making sure markets function well, by reducing and preventing financial crime.

topChunk.chunkText: 17 Annex 3Compatibility statementCompliance with legal requirements1. This Annex records the FCA’s compliance with a number of legal requirements applicable to the proposals in this consultation, including an explanation of the FCA’s reasons for concluding that our proposals in this consultation are compatible with certain requirements under the Financial Services and Markets Act 2000 (FSMA). 2. Section 1B(1) of FSMA requires that the FCA, when discharging its general functions, as far as reasonably possible, act in a way which is compatible with its strategic objective and advances one or more of its operational objectives, and its general duty under section 1B(5)(a) of FSMA to have regard to the regulatory principles in section 3B of FSMA.3. This Annex also sets out the FCA’s view of how the proposed rules are compatible with the duty on the FCA to discharge its general functions (which include rule-making) in a way which promotes effective competition in the interests of consumers (section 1B(4)). This duty applies in so far as promoting competition is compatible with advancing the FCA’s consumer protection and/or integrity objectives. 4. In addition, we have considered the recommendations made by the Treasury under s 1JA FSMA about aspects of the economic policy of His Majesty’s Government to which we should have regard in connection with our general duties. 5. This Annex includes our assessment of the equality and diversity implications of these proposals. The FCA’s objectives and regulatory principles: Compatibility statement6. The proposals set out in this consultation are primarily intended to advance the FCA’s operational objective of ensuring that the relevant markets function well. Changes are also relevant to the FCA’s integrity and consumer protection objectives.7. We consider these proposals are compatible with the FCA’s strategic objective of ensuring that the relevant markets function well, through reducing and preventing financial crime. The consultation aligns with our objective to publish findings from our reviews and provide feedback to industry on what we see, so firms can improve their controls.8. We are confident that the new guidance is compatible with our secondary international competitiveness and growth objective.
